question: Is the parastatal's territorial/geographic jurisdiction specifically defined in it's enabling law?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Not determined. The sources show that BDA's jurisdiction is set by notification and not fixed in the Act, but the Citation Sheet has no notification that fixes the current boundary. | EVIDENCE: (1) BDA-08, ODA (P&BS) Rules 2020, rule 1(2): the Rules 'extend to all the "development areas" which are so declared under sub- section (1) of Section 3 of the Odisha Development Authorities Act., 1982'. So the area is declared by notification under s.3(1) and is not described in the Act. (2) BDA-09, BDA Regulations 2022, reg. 1(2): they apply to 'the whole area within the jurisdiction of Bhubaneswar Development Authority as notified from time to time'. This confirms the area is set by notification and gives no boundary. (3) BDA-03, Annual Report 2026, p.23: the Authority 'approved 143 nos. of revenue villages identified by BDA for inclusion within administrative jurisdiction of BDA covering 239.58 Sqkm' and 'the said proposal has been sent to Government for further notification'. This extension is proposed and not yet notified. (4) BDA-06 is a map and village list titled 'MAP SHOWING THE VILLAGES PROPOSED FOR EXTENTION OF BDA AREA', and it labels both 'Existing BDA Area' and 'Extention BDA Area'. It is a BDA plan and not a legal notification. | CAVEATS: The enabling law points to a legally identifiable territorial definition, namely the area notified under s.3(1). The actual s.3 notification and the Odisha Gazette text defining the existing BDA area are not in the sheet. The m
quote: They shall extend to all the “development areas” which are so declared under sub- section (1) of Section 3 of the Odisha Development Authorities Act., 1982.
comments: I left the score blank. The Rules and the BDA Regulations 2022 (reg. 1(2)) both say the area is declared by notification under s.3(1) of the ODA Act, 1982. That points to a legally identifiable notified area, which fits the Score 5 wording. I could not confirm it, though. The Citation Sheet has no ODA Act s.3 text and no gazette notification of the BDA development area. BDA-06 is a BDA map of proposed village extensions and is not a legal notification. BDA-03 says the 143-village extension was only sent to Government for notification. A score of 0 needs affirmative absence, and that is not established. The team should obtain the s.3 notification for the existing BDA area. If the Act or notification defines it, the score would be 5. I have not read the full text of the other sheet sources, which include BDA-09, BDA-03, BDA-06 and BDA-10. This is based on the Step 2 summary and BDA-08.

question: Does the ULG have representation on the parastatal's governing board?

The Chairpersons of Khurda and Jatni Municipalities are also listed as ex-officio members. The BMC Commissioner appears only under 'Special Invitees'. No source in the sheet says whether these members have voting rights. The enabling ODA Act, 1982 composition clause is not in the Citation Sheet, so I cannot confirm voting rights from the law. I have not scored. | EVIDENCE: Annual Report 2026 (BDA-03), p.14, 'THE AUTHORITY' chart. Members: Official = Additional Chief Secretary H&UD, Engineer Member, Finance & Accounts Member, Town & Regional Planning Member, Member Estate, Member Environment, Member Enforcement. Non-official = '1. Mayor, BMC, Member Ex-Officio 2. Chairperson, Khurda Municipality Member Ex-Officio 3. Chairman, Jatni Municipality Member Ex-Officio'. Special Invitees = Director Town Planning, RDC Central Division, Director Estate GA Dept., Collector Khurda, Commissioner BMC. The ODA (P&BS) Rules 2020 (BDA-08, Rule on the DP and BP Committee) put the BMC Commissioner on that committee as Vice-Chairman. That is a sub-committee, not the governing board. | CAVEATS: The Mayor is an elected ULG representative and is shown as a 'Member', not an invitee. That points towards Score 5, but voting rights are not stated in the sheet. The BMC Commissioner is an invitee only. The Annual Report is a secondary, administrativ
comments: The BDA Annual Report 2026 (BDA-03, p.14) lists the Mayor of BMC as a 'Member Ex-Officio' on the Authority. The Mayor is an elected ULG representative. The Chairpersons of the Khurda and Jatni municipalities are also listed as ex-officio members. The BMC Commissioner appears only under 'Special Invitees'. The report does not say whether members vote. The Odisha Development Authorities Act 1982 composition clause (section 5) is not in the Citation Sheet. A follow-up search of the sheet found only the ODA (P&BS) Rules 2020, which do not cover board composition. The Odisha Municipal Corporation Act is also not in the sheet. Score 5 needs voting rights confirmed and 2.5 needs them shown to be absent, so I have left the score blank. Absence is not shown either, so 0 does not apply. A reviewer should check the ODA Act 1982 section on constitution of the Authority and members' voting rights. BDA-03 is an administrative report with no effective date, so it cannot be shown to be in force on 31 Aug 2026. If voting rights are confirmed, the score is likely 5.
